task.title: Draw a full-width title strip the window drags by
task.description:
PR #161 made the sidebar head the window's grab handle on macOS, which leaves the top of the board area, most of the window's width, non-draggable. Dylan wants what every Mac and Windows app has: the whole top edge moves the window. The board area is a separate WebContentsView drawn by the Go board page, so the shell has to own that strip.

Add a title strip to the chrome across the top of the main area, drawn by the shell: the height of the platform's window-control row (34px on macOS to line up with the traffic-light inset the sidebar head already uses, 36px on Windows to match the titleBarOverlay, none on Linux where native decorations remain), marked -webkit-app-region: drag, showing the active project's name (or the app name when none) centered in muted type, following the theme. The board views are laid out below it: boardBounds() gains the strip's height in y and loses it in height, and the chrome's own main-column views start under it. The sidebar head keeps its drag region so the two form one continuous bar. On Windows keep the title out from under the window-controls overlay (the overlay exposes env(titlebar-area-width) and friends to the page). One strip height constant shared by the main process and the renderer. Tests: the bounds math as a pure function, the strip's drag rule and theme tokens in the stylesheet test. Supersedes the sidebar-only decision recorded on the previous task.
